result.summary: The landlord did the smoke alarm and socket repairs himself and says they were finished on 31 Aug. None of it is verified, and he mentions fixing only one socket after the tenant's report of several loose sockets. I've asked the tenant to confirm the alarm works and all sockets are secure, with a hold to chase in 3 days. I've asked the landlord for the alarm's make and model or a photo, and whether any other sockets were checked. I've recorded the facts and passed the safety and compliance angle to a person at normal priority. The ticket isn't closed yet.
result.situation: The tenant removed a beeping landing smoke alarm, leaving a ceiling opening, and had reported several loose sockets. The landlord declined an agency contractor and did the work himself. He now says it's complete and asks for the property record to be updated.

judgement.why_this_decision: The landlord's completion claim (events 012 and 014) is unverified. A working smoke alarm on each floor is a legal requirement. The tenant reported several loose sockets (event 005), but the landlord mentions only one fix after the report; the kitchen one was 5 Aug, before it. Jev gave a safety concern of 0.76. The tenant can confirm all of this directly, so I asked her before closing. I escalated because DIY electrical work and a possible damp issue (the dehumidifier) need agency judgement.

alternatives_considered.option: Close the ticket on the landlord's word
alternatives_considered.why_not: It's safety-critical compliance work with no evidence, and the sockets may only be partly fixed.
The landlord declined agency contractors and nothing is approved. I offered to arrange one with his approval instead.
No live hazard has been confirmed, and the landlord says the alarm is fitted. The tenant has safe-use advice meanwhile.
